previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and tobacco use, was admitted with three days of chest pressure at rest and worsening shortness of breath. He had a recent echocardiogram showing severely reduced ejection fraction, consistent with ischemic cardiomyopathy. In the hospital, he was treated for acute on chronic systolic heart failure and unstable angina. A cardiac catheterization revealed a 60% blockage in the left circumflex artery, but due to its retroflexed anatomy, further intervention was not performed. He was managed medically with initiation of lisinopril, metoprolol, atorvastatin, furosemide, and spironolactone. Metformin was held pending renal function testing. He improved clinically and was discharged home in stable condition with clear instructions for follow-up, lab monitoring, and medication adjustments.
